newsitem.title: UK: Cortecs pushes back data collection to Jan.
newsitem.headline: Cortecs pushes back data collection to Jan.

text.p: British-based drug development firm Cortecs International Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to push back the collection of data for its oral calcitonin product to January instead of December.
The company said it had completed a trial involving healthy elderly volunteers to evaluate the excretion of bone breakdown markers over a 48-hour period.
Oral calcitonin is a therapy for the prevention of bone breakdown currently in Phase I/II trials.

"The unexpectedly large diurnal fluctuations of bone marker excretion and an average bone turnover some three times higher than in young healthy adults indicate that repeated dose studies on bone marker excretion will be the most preferable route to the company's registration application," Cortecs said.
The company added in a statement that about 180 patients would provide data from repeated dose studies during January.
Cortecs said it expected to use that data as pivotal information for European submission rather than a single large-dose response trial which will be completed in December.
Cortecs' shares fell 14p to 191.5p by 1045 GMT.
Regarding its other products, Cortecs said its oral insulin programme for diabetic patients was on schedule following the completion of the second stage of the Phase I trial.

The company said results from the study, which included six healthy subjects, showed that mean insulin level increases in the blood following the administration of oral insulin were greater than after the placebo and also declined more slowly.

"We are very pleased with these latest results and are now proceeding carefully to the next stage, which will include diabetic patients," the company said, adding that it planned further trials in early 1997.
